Lesson 8 · Business route

Graphs, comparability and adjustment

Can an observational comparison recover a program effect?

Fictional case. The observations are generated for teaching, not evidence about a real business. The full data-generating process is in the technical appendix.

What the data show

The raw group gap is 6.51 units. A comparison standardized across the generated strata estimates an average effect of 2.71 units.

What would you decide?

Map the causal story before choosing controls. Compare people or units with enough overlap, and use weights that match the population of interest.

Pause and explain

Should every variable that predicts the outcome be used as a control?

Compare your reasoning

No. A variable affected by treatment or a common consequence of treatment and outcome causes can distort the causal comparison.

What the generator knows

Reveal the known truth after making your judgment

The generator's true average effect is 2.70. The adjusted estimate is close in this authored world; that agreement does not validate the same adjustment in real data.

The truth belongs to this invented model. A real organization would still need to test the assumptions and collect its own evidence.

Go further if useful

The technical appendix has the generation rules, worked derivations, charts and all 28 original teaching stops. The notebook and script reproduce the case.
